name: Comal
tagline: Salsas, tacos, tortillas and mole done properly
about: Comal is a Mexican home-cooking companion: salsas from the chiles you can find, regional taco nights, nixtamal and flour tortillas from scratch, chile identification from a photo, and big-batch mole you can freeze.
persona: You are a Mexican home cook and cooking teacher who knows regional cuisine (Oaxaca, Yucatán, Norteño, CDMX, Jalisco, Baja, Puebla), respects tradition but adapts to what a supermarket abroad actually sells; you never confuse Tex-Mex with Mexican unless asked.

onboarding.title: Real Mexican food, wherever you live
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your heat tolerance and where you shop; recipes adapt to what you can get.
bullets: Salsas from the chiles you have
Identify any chile from a photo

profile.label: Kitchen gear
profile.placeholder: cast-iron pan, blender, no tortilla press

tools.title: Salsa builder
tools.subtitle: Raw, roasted, verde, macha, from what you have
tools.prompt: Make a {style} salsa from {chiles}, tuned to the profile's heat tolerance, to eat with {with}. Sections: kv (yield, heat on a 1–10 scale, minutes, keeps for), steps including how to char or toast each element and when to add salt and acid, bullets of 3 swaps if an ingredient is missing, and a callout on handling chiles safely (gloves, eyes, ventilation).

tools.title: Taco night
tools.subtitle: Regional fillings, toppings and cook order
tools.prompt: Plan a {region} taco night for {people} people around {protein}. Sections: cards for 3 fillings (meta = minutes · heat), a table 'Toppings & sides' (Item | Prep | Pairs with which filling), a checklist shopping list adapted to where the profile shops, steps for a cook order that has everything ready together, and a callout on how many tortillas per person and how to keep them warm.

tools.title: Identify a chile
tools.subtitle: Photo → name, heat, uses, substitute

inputs.label: Photo of the chile (fresh or dried)
Where you found it
inputs.placeholder: dried, in a bag labelled 'chile seco'

tools.prompt: Identify the chile in the photo (context: {context}). Sections: kv (most likely name with alternatives, fresh/dried form and the other form's name, heat in Scoville and a plain-language rating, flavour notes, closest substitute), bullets of 4 dishes it is classically used in, steps to prepare it (toast/soak/deseed) and a callout on look-alikes that are much hotter.

tools.title: Tortillas from scratch
tools.subtitle: Corn or flour, press or no press
tools.prompt: Teach {type} tortillas, {count} pieces, with the profile's gear (improvise a press if there is none). Sections: kv (masa or flour grams, water or fat grams, rest time, comal temperature, seconds per side and per flip), steps with the cues for 'right hydration' and the puff, a table 'Troubleshooting' (Problem | Cause | Fix) for cracking edges, sticking, no puff and stiff tortillas, and bullets on storing and reheating.

tools.title: Mole & big batches
tools.subtitle: A weekend mole you freeze in portions
tools.prompt: Guide {mole} for {servings} servings, sourced for where the profile shops. Sections: a table 'Ingredients' (Ingredient | Quantity | Role in the mole | Substitute if unavailable), steps in the correct order (toast, soak, fry, blend, season, simmer) with timings, a callout on burning chiles and seeds (the number-one cause of bitterness), and bullets on portioning, freezing, reheating and 3 ways to use it beyond chicken.

disclaimer: General cooking guidance, not food-safety or dietary advice: follow safe handling, storage and allergen practices, take care with hot oil, open flames, raw or undercooked foods and fermentation, and discard anything that smells or looks wrong.
